newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-PRESIDENT ADDS NO CLARITY ON ELECTION PLANS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-PRESIDENT ADDS NO CLARITY ON ELECTION PLANS.

text.p: Responding to media reports that quoted him as saying his generation's time of leadership had passed, President Algirdas Brasauskas said on Monday that this did not pertain to the December presidential elections.

"My statement, if you have in mind the words `older generation,' has nothing to do with the elections," Brazauskas, who will turn 65 in September, told reporters. "I didn't mention the elections as such."
Lithuanian media carried accounts of Brazauskas' statement, which was reported last week in Poland's Rzeczpospolita, over the weekend.
The statement was the subject of speculation that Brazauskas would not stand for reelection this year.
Brazauskas has yet to announce his intentions.
Brazauskas said that he had been speaking more broadly about the level of political culture in Lithuania, which he said was on a low level and was still marked by Soviet-era education.
"We have to see people emerging in our society free from all those Marxist ideas," Brazauskas, the former head of Lithuania's Communist Party, said.
The head of state refused to say whether he would run for a second, five-year term.
"I'm going to answer this question in due time," Brazauskas said.
